reason: Comparison with the Cambridge copy corrected the first reading's 'fructus sue patientie', 'vapores ignis' and 'pellyparius de fructu' to 'vere patientie', 'vapores incendij' and 'pellyparius defuncto', and confirmed the expansions of the abbreviated framing formulas.
sources: Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS 327, ff. 175v-176r, 179v-180v, section IV of the compilation, page images Parker on the Web, purl.stanford.edu/kb304wh5721

M. R. James, A Descriptive Catalogue of the Manuscripts in the Library of Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, vol. II (Cambridge 1912), pp. 146-148, MS 327 item 3: 'Opusculum compilatum de libris sanctorum patrum', prologue 'In consequenti opusculo ordinantur', 20 sections

H. L. D. Ward and J. A. Herbert, Catalogue of Romances in the Department of Manuscripts in the British Museum, vol. III (London 1910), pp. 696-698, Sloane 4029 ff. 184-259: headings De sancta Maria, De sancta Cruce, De bonis angelis, De Sanctis Dei; Hugh of St Victor exemplum f. 200b
Les Enluminures, Textmanuscripts TM 427, description (2010): section list of a northern Italian copy, and the Florence BNCF Conv. Soppr. D.8.1128 copy (not seen)
Gregory the Great, Dialogi I.9 and III.15, and Hugh of St Victor, De sacramentis II.xvi.2, as sources of single chapters (not the containing work)
